items.label: Aims
items.prompt: The INTRODUCTION ends with two aims. Find the FIRST one.
items.model: To explore how demographic factors influence phone addiction, procrastination and achievement among medical students.
items.why: There are actually three 'aimed to' sentences in the Introduction; the final pair at the end states the study's aims.

items.label: Second aim
items.prompt: Find the SECOND aim (about relationships between the main variables).
items.model: To explore the association between mobile phone addiction, academic procrastination and academic achievement.
items.why: 'We further explored…' adds the second aim.

items.label: Hypothesis
items.prompt: Does the article state a formal hypothesis?
items.model: No. There are only aims; the expected direction is implied by past studies but never stated as a prediction.
items.why: Past research suggesting a negative link is not the same as the authors stating a hypothesis.

items.label: Predictors and outcome
items.prompt: In the regression, what are the two main predictors and the outcome?
items.model: Predictors: mobile phone addiction and academic procrastination. Outcome: academic achievement (4 dimensions).
items.why: The hierarchical regression examined their influence on academic achievement after controlling for demographics.

items.label: Conceptual definition (phone addiction)
items.prompt: Find the conceptual definition of MOBILE PHONE ADDICTION.
items.model: The uncontrolled use of mobile phones in inappropriate or harmful situations.
items.why: '…is defined as…' signals the conceptual definition.

items.label: Conceptual definition (procrastination)
items.prompt: Find the conceptual definition of ACADEMIC PROCRASTINATION.
items.model: An intentional delay in the learning process and intended course; a type of situational procrastination.
items.why: Each main variable is defined in its own part of the Introduction.

items.label: Conceptual definition (achievement)
items.prompt: Find the conceptual definition of ACADEMIC ACHIEVEMENT.
items.model: The sum of medical students' learning consequences, attitudes and behaviours (behavioural performance + objective achievement).
items.why: It appears early, before the other two definitions.

items.label: Operational definition (procrastination)
items.prompt: How was academic procrastination measured? Find the sentence naming the scale.
items.model: Academic Procrastination Scale–Short (APS-S): 5 items on a 5-point scale.
items.why: The Measures subsection names the scale and explains its scoring.

items.label: Reliability
items.prompt: Find the sentence reporting the reliability of the phone addiction scale IN THIS STUDY.
items.model: Cronbach's α = 0.825 in this study.
items.why: Two earlier alphas come from OTHER studies; 'In this study' tells you which one belongs to the current sample.

items.label: General method
items.prompt: What general method did this study use?
items.model: A cross-sectional online questionnaire survey.
items.why: One survey at one time point; no manipulation.

items.label: Sampling
items.prompt: Find the sentence describing the SAMPLING method.
items.model: Multistage stratified convenience sampling; participants from different classes and grades were randomly selected.
items.why: Sampling method is in the Study Design and Procedures subsection.

items.label: Sample
items.prompt: How many VALID questionnaires were analysed, and what was the response rate?
items.model: 3,511 valid questionnaires (effective response rate 81.7%).
items.why: 5,921 were distributed and 4,297 returned, but only 3,511 were valid after exclusions.

items.label: Exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Find the EXCLUSION criteria (data-quality checks).
items.model: Taking under 8 minutes, or answering quality-control questions incorrectly.
items.why: These checks remove careless responses.

items.label: Research gap
items.prompt: Find the sentence stating the research gap about procrastination.
items.model: Few studies directly explored procrastination and achievement among Chinese medical students.
items.why: 'However, few studies have…' signals a gap.

items.label: Control variables
items.prompt: Find the sentence showing that demographic variables were CONTROLLED for in the regression.
items.model: Hierarchical regression examined phone addiction and procrastination after controlling for demographics.
items.why: In hierarchical regression, control variables are entered first.

items.label: Unexpected result
items.prompt: Find the sentence reporting that phone addiction was NOT related to one achievement dimension.
items.model: Phone addiction did not affect objective achievement.
items.why: Compare the Results: phone addiction predicted 3 dimensions; procrastination predicted all 4.

items.label: Overclaiming
items.prompt: The design is cross-sectional. Find a sentence in the DISCUSSION that uses CAUSAL language anyway.
items.model: '…mobile phone addiction HAS A NEGATIVE IMPACT on learning dedication…'
items.why: 'Impact' and 'influence' imply cause. The authors admit in their limitations that the design can't show causation, so this is overclaiming.

items.label: Practical implication
items.prompt: Find a practical recommendation for INSTRUCTORS.
items.model: Guide students to reduce procrastination and hold regular face-to-face talks with phone-addicted students.
items.why: Implications for medical education are written as recommendations.

items.label: Limitation (generalisability)
items.prompt: Find the FIRST limitation.
items.model: Participants came from four medical schools in one province, limiting generalisability.
items.why: Limitations are numbered First, Additionally, Finally.

items.label: Limitation (measures)
items.prompt: Find the limitation about the MEASURES.
items.model: Several scales were developed for Western samples and need more attention in the Chinese context.
items.why: This is about cultural validity of the measures.

items.label: Limitation (design)
items.prompt: Find the limitation about the DESIGN.
items.model: Cross-sectional, so it can't explain causal relationships.
items.why: Notice how this contradicts the causal wording used elsewhere in the paper.
